requirement_text: The organization must determine the internal and external issues that affect its ability to achieve the intended outcomes of its AI management system. These issues must include AI-specific risks and opportunities.
Top management must demonstrate leadership and commitment to the AI management system by ensuring AI policy is established and aligned with organizational strategy.
An AI policy must be established, implemented, and maintained. The policy must include commitments to comply with requirements and continually improve the AI management system.
Roles, responsibilities, and authorities for AI system-related roles must be assigned, communicated, and maintained. An AI management system owner must be designated.
The organization must plan and implement a risk assessment process for AI systems. Risks must be identified, analyzed, evaluated, and treated according to the organization's risk criteria.
AI risk treatment options must be selected and implemented. Treatment plans must include controls, responsibilities, timelines, and verification of effectiveness.
The organization must determine and provide the resources needed for the establishment, implementation, maintenance, and continual improvement of the AI management system.
The organization must determine the necessary competence of persons doing work that affects AI system performance and ensure they are competent on the basis of education, training, or experience.
Persons doing work under the organization's control must be aware of the AI policy, their contribution to the AI management system, and the implications of not conforming to requirements.
The organization must determine the need for internal and external communications relevant to the AI management system, including what, when, with whom, and how to communicate.
The AI management system must include documented information required by the standard and determined by the organization as necessary for effectiveness.
The organization must plan, implement, and control the processes needed to meet AI system requirements. This includes establishing criteria for AI system processes and implementing controls.
The organization must establish requirements for AI systems. Requirements must address functionality, performance, safety, security, privacy, and ethical considerations.
The organization must establish and maintain processes for data management relevant to AI systems. This includes data acquisition, quality, provenance, preparation, and governance.
The organization must establish processes for AI system development, including design, training, testing, and validation. Development processes must be documented and controlled.
The organization must establish and maintain processes for AI system deployment. Deployment must include verification, validation, and confirmation that the system meets requirements.
The organization must establish and maintain processes for AI system operation and monitoring. This includes performance tracking, incident management, and change control.
The organization must monitor, measure, analyze, and evaluate the AI management system. Internal audits must be conducted at planned intervals.
Top management must review the AI management system at planned intervals to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness.
The organization must continually improve the suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness of the AI management system. Nonconformities must be corrected and their causes addressed.
The organization must establish data governance processes for AI systems including data classification, data quality assessment, data lineage tracking, and data retention policies.
Security controls specific to AI systems must be implemented including model access control, inference security, prompt injection prevention, and output filtering.
AI system monitoring must include model drift detection, data drift detection, bias monitoring, performance degradation tracking, and security event detection.

AI impact assessment must be conducted to evaluate potential impacts on individuals, society, and the organization. Assessment must cover fundamental rights, safety, privacy, and ethical implications.
